# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 69 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 69 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_069_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 7 — Repentance and Its Limits

**69:1** After I had seen all these things I said to him: "Lord, I wish to know one more thing about those who repent." "Speak," he said. "Is the repentance of all who repent beneficial — does their repentance secure life for them before the Lord?" "All who repent with their whole heart," he said, "and who cleanse themselves from all the wickedness I have described, and who add no more sins to their previous ones — these obtain healing from their previous sins, provided they are not double-minded about these commandments. And they shall live to God."

**69:2** "But those who do not repent and persist in their pleasures," I said, "will they obtain life?" "They shall not," he said.

**69:3** "But, lord, I have heard from certain teachers," I said, "that there is no repentance other than the one given at the water of baptism." "That is true," he said. "So it stands. For one who has received forgiveness of sins ought never to sin again, but to live in purity. Since, however, you inquire precisely about all things, I will explain this to you as well — not in order to give excuse to those who are going to believe, or who have already believed, in the Lord."

**69:4** "For those who have already believed, or who shall believe hereafter, do not have repentance for sins — they have forgiveness of their former sins. But for those who were called before and sinned, there is the possibility of repentance. And this repentance, as I have said, is unique and final. For the same person is not to repent repeatedly."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the once-for-all repentance doctrine.*
